critical_code_review_comments: drive.save_settings: PUT /api/drive/settings returns {checked: bool(svc)} — when Drive IS connected the DriveWriter(svc, parts).folder(parts) call will raise RuntimeError('Drive folder not found: My Drive/...') for a non-existent path and is caught -> 400. Good. But when Drive is NOT connected the folder is saved without any sanity check (even nonsense like 'a/////b' becomes 'a/b' due to split_path). Acceptable because split_path strips empties.

routes.recrop sets db.sets.{set_id}.drive = null directly instead of using set_drive, which skips the drive.* nested helper. Correct behaviour but inconsistent with set_drive() elsewhere; a future refactor should use a single helper.

routes.recrop_set uses done_qp_jobs() which scans every done set, loads all their jobs just to find one. For 2 sets it's fine; at 1000+ sets consider a direct db.jobs.find_one({set_id, doc_type:'question_paper', status:'done', is_deleted:False}) + db.sets.find_one.

routes.recrop empties qp.questions and resets status='ready' but does NOT invalidate the stored page_paths/page_masks on the QP job. Those are reused by the AI stage so this is correct, but worth a comment because status='ready' means refresh_set re-queues cropping only (not re-rasterization). Good.

drive.split_path: body.root_path='////My Drive/////a' -> ['My Drive','a'] because only the FIRST leading 'My Drive/' is stripped. If a user pastes 'My Drive/My Drive/Foo' they get root ['My Drive','Foo']. Minor UX quirk; consider stripping repeatedly or validating.
